title: Destructive Time Optimization™
summary: Saving time now by spending the future's component budget.
definition: The engineering philosophy of sacrificing potentially useful components to save time in the present, with complete disregard for the possibility that they might be useful later.
examples: We cut the female Dupont wires instead of exploring alternative connection methods because cutting them took less time.
known_side_effects: Future regret, reduced component availability, and a disappointed engineering partner.
origin: A disagreement over whether female Dupont wires should have been cut before exploring other options.
philosophical_justification: Why preserve a component for an uncertain future when you can eliminate the problem immediately?
warning: Time saved is temporary. The consequences may persist until the next component order arrives.
